title: The Agentic SecOps Platform admin portal: supported browsers, egress IPs, status board, account settings, failure emails, AI capabilities and audit logs
aliases: Agentic Security Operations Platform Admin Portal

prose.label: Egress addresses.
prose.text: {{public-ips}} The EU entry is worded differently on the Azure Blob connector page {{divergence:eu-egress-pointer}}.

prose.label: Subjects under this portal.
prose.text: Roles, users and content permissions are in [[unified.secops-platform.console.access-control]]. Entity-page filters, columns, grouping, drawers, saved views, tickets and formatting rules are in [[unified.secops-platform.console.entity-views]]. Playbooks and automation rules are in [[unified.secops-platform.console.automation]]. Historical data is in [[unified.secops-platform.console.historical-data]]. Custom dashboards, widgets and reports are in [[unified.secops-platform.console.dashboards-reports]]. Log search, the Queries Library and Entity Explorer are in [[unified.secops-platform.console.explore]]. The Users page and user details drawer are in [[unified.secops-platform.console.users]].

browsers.statement: The admin portal is actively tested on the two most recent versions of Safari, Chrome, Edge and Firefox; older versions of these and other browsers are expected to work but are not actively tested.

quotes: Zscaler actively tests browser compatibility with the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal.
Apple Safari (two most recent versions)
Google Chrome (two most recent versions)
Microsoft Edge (two most recent versions)
Mozilla Firefox (two most recent versions)
Older versions of these browsers should be compatible, but are no longer actively tested.
Other browsers should be compatible, but are not actively tested.

public-ips.statement: The page says the listed addresses are the source of all egress traffic from the Zscaler tenant for the platform and its applications (e.g. UVM, AEM); the US region lists three /32 addresses, and for the EU region the page points to the Zscaler Hub IP Addresses list.

quotes: These IP addresses serve as the source for all egress traffic originating from the Zscaler tenant.
| EU | The recommended IP addresses listed in Zscaler Hub IP Addresses |
allowlist the public IP addresses used by outgoing traffic from the Agentic Security Operations Platform (Agentic SecOps Platform) and its applications (e.g., UVM, AEM, etc.)

status-board.statement: The platform status board presents historic and current incidents and lets you report issues, subscribe to updates and feeds, see the current status of the admin portal, and view incident history and historical uptime.

quotes: The status board presents historic and current incidents.
Report issues.
Subscribe to updates and feeds.
View the current status of the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal.
View incident history and historical uptime.

account-general.statement: Account Settings > General Settings holds the tenant name and account type, a logo (JPG, GIF or PNG), the organization email domain, and two checkboxes: one lets all admins view private dashboards and reports, the other lets viewers change dashboard-level filters but not save them.

quotes: Name: Displays the name of the tenant account that you logged in to.
Account Logo: Upload a logo for the account. The supported file formats are JPG, GIF, and PNG.
Email Domain: Enter your organization's email domain.
Allow Admins to view private dashboards and reports: Select the checkbox to allow all admins in the account to view private dashboards.
Allow viewers to change dashboard level filters by default: Select the checkbox to allow all viewers to modify dashboard filters on the Edit Dashboards page.
If selected, viewers can apply filters to analyze dashboard data, but they cannot save the filters.
Account Type: Displays the account type.

account-authentication.statement: The Authenticate section of Account Settings offers two authentication types for users of the tenant: SAML through an identity provider, or username and password.

quotes: Authentication Type: Select the authentication method to authenticate users accessing this tenant.
SAML: Users can authenticate through a SAML-based identity provider (IdP).
Username & Password: Users can authenticate with their username and password.

failure-email-prerequisite.statement: Failure email notifications are set in the Email Notifications section of Profile Settings and require a role with Edit permission under the Platform - Outegrations resource.

quotes: click the Profile menu in the top navigation bar, and click Profile Settings.
In the Email Notifications section:
your assigned role must include the Edit permissions under the Platform - Outegrations resource

failure-email-alert-types.statement: Failure notifications can be enabled for three alert types: source runs (which fail for causes such as API rate limits, expired or invalid credentials, schema changes or upstream outages), ETL and data pipeline processing (data type mismatches, out-of-range or invalid values), and outegrations (for example expired Jira tokens stopping ticket creation).

quotes: Source runs fail for various reasons, including API rate limits, expired or invalid credentials, schema changes, or upstream outages.
ETL and data pipeline processes can fail when data manipulation encounters errors such as data type mismatches, out-of-range values, invalid values, etc.
Failures can occur during third-party outegrations. For example, expired tokens for Jira can stop tickets from being created.

failure-email-schedule.statement: Failure notification emails default to Daily and the frequency cannot be modified; the delivery time is set in the admin's local time, and the email goes to the address of the admin who enabled the notifications.

quotes: Frequency: The default setting is Daily. This setting cannot be modified.
Time: Set the local time you want the email delivered (based on your time zone).
Emails are sent at the configured time to the email address associated with the admin who enabled the notifications.

ai-capabilities-toggle.statement: AI capabilities (for example Remediation Copilot and Mapping Copilot) are switched on or off with Enable AI Capabilities in Account Settings, and the change applies at the account level to all users.

quotes: AI-powered tools (e.g., Remediation Copilot, Mapping Copilot)
select or deselect Enable AI Capabilities to opt in or out of AI features
Opting in or out of AI capabilities applies the change at the account level and makes them available or unavailable to all users within the platform.
click the Profile menu in the top navigation bar, and click Account Settings.

ai-capabilities-privacy.statement: The page says AI capabilities process data within Zscaler's secured services without using it to train the underlying models and without sending it to external third parties, and that the system attempts to strip PII before processing, so users should still be cautious with sensitive information.

quotes: process data entirely within Zscaler's secured services and are not used to train the underlying AI models
The data is not transmitted to external third parties and is protected by encryption and strict access controls.
Though the system attempts to strip personally identifiable information (PII) before processing, users should exercise caution with sensitive information.

audit-log-events.statement: Audit logs record user-initiated actions, including changes to grouping rules, severity, score and SLA settings, roles and content permissions, UI configurations, account and user settings, data source mapping, instances and scheduling, outegrations, and dashboards and reports.

quotes: Audit logs track user-initiated actions within the Agentic Security Operations Platform
Configuration of grouping rules and rule sets.
Configuration of severity, score, and SLA settings.
Creating, managing, and assigning roles and content permissions.
Configuring UI configurations.
Updates to account settings and user settings.
Management of data source mapping, data source instances, and data source scheduling.
Configuration and mapping of outegrations.
Changes to dashboards and reports.

audit-log-retention.statement: Audit logs are retained for 90 days; to extend retention the logs can be exported to an Amazon S3 bucket or any other configured log destination.

quotes: Audit logs are retained for 90 days.
To extend the retention period and to maintain a long-term history, you can export the logs to an Amazon S3 bucket or any other configured log destination.

audit-log-page.statement: Audit logs are opened from the More menu of a user, account, source, outegration or report configuration page (for SOC Workbench from Settings > Scoring, Severity or UI Config); the Audit Logs page for a user can be filtered and sorted by operation, type and user name and downloaded as CSV.

quotes: For a source: Go to Configure > Sources, then click a source.
For an outegration: Go to Configure > Outegrations, then click an outegration.
For SOC Workbench only: Go to Settings > Scoring, Settings > Severity, or Settings > UI Config.
Filter and sort the logs by operation, type, and user name.
Download the logs as a CSV file.
For a user: Click the Profile menu in the top navigation bar, then click Profile Settings.
For an account: Click the Profile menu in the top navigation bar, then click Account Settings.
For a report: Go to an application in the top navigation bar (Vulnerabilities, Assets, etc.), click My Reports, and click a report.
Click the More menu, and click Audit Logs.
On the Audit Logs page for a user, you can do the following:

audit-log-export.statement: Audit log export is scheduled in the Audit Logs Export section, reached through Profile menu > Account Settings although the page introduces the steps as being 'for a user', with Enable Scheduling, the entity types to include, a Daily or Hourly frequency and a storage outegration as the destination.

evidence.after: To configure automated audit log export for a user:
quotes: Click the Profile menu in the top navigation bar, then click Account Settings.
To configure automated audit log export for a user:
You can schedule audit logs to be sent on a daily or hourly basis via an outegration.
Included Entities: Select the entity types to be included in the audit log
Frequency: Define the time interval for the audit log export (e.g., Daily or Hourly).
Select Storage Outegration: Choose a destination for the audit log export.
In the Audit Logs Export section:
Select Enable Scheduling.

signin-article-outline.statement: The sign-in article lists three topics: signing in, accessing the Admin Settings and navigating within the admin portal.

quotes: Signing In to the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal
Accessing the Admin Settings
Navigating within the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal

signin-outline-only.title: How an admin signs in and navigates the admin portal
signin-outline-only.detail: The captured sign-in article is an outline of three topics (signing in, accessing the Admin Settings, navigating within the portal); the sign-in method, URL and navigation structure are not in the capture.

audit-log-retention-scope.title: Whether playbook and automation-rule audit logs share the 90-day retention
audit-log-retention-scope.detail: The account audit log page says logs are retained for 90 days. The playbook and automation-rule pages say only that their Download icon downloads the logs of the last 90 days. No captured page says whether those logs share the retention.

account-type-values.title: What the Account Type values are and what viewing private dashboards means for non-admins
account-type-values.detail: The Account Settings page says Account Type 'Displays the account type' without listing values, and does not say what Allow Admins to view private dashboards and reports means for users who are not admins.

eu-egress-pointer.summary: Both pages list the same three US egress addresses, but for the EU the public IP addresses page points to the Zscaler Hub IP Addresses list while the Azure Blob connector page says 'Refer to the Zscaler Config.'

positions.says: The EU addresses are the recommended IP addresses listed in Zscaler Hub IP Addresses.

quotes: | EU | The recommended IP addresses listed in Zscaler Hub IP Addresses |

positions.says: The EU addresses are found by referring to the Zscaler Config.

quotes: | EU | Refer to the Zscaler Config. |

eu-egress-pointer.impact: It is unclear whether the two pages point to the same EU address list; an allowlist for the EU region should not rest on either wording alone.
